prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1190; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed head-on collision. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Police report obtained and confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The other driver and two independent witnesses describe the accident in the same way the claimant did.

Entry 3: Photographs of the damage reviewed. The front-end damage to the claimant's vehicle lines up with the impact described and with the other vehicle's damage.

Entry 4: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force on the date of loss. Nothing in the file points to earlier damage to the vehicle, and the damage appears to have occurred on the reported date.

Entry 5: Counsel submitted the medical summary showing a shoulder injury. The type of injury and the force of the crash are consistent with each other.

Entry 6: Records show no prior treatment or complaints involving the same shoulder. Recovery has taken somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of injury, so the treating provider's notes are being reviewed.

Entry 7: Claimant gave a recorded statement through counsel. The account matches what was given at first notice and in every later conversation.

Entry 8: Reviewed the treatment timeline with the medical reviewer. Duration is longer than usual, but the provider has documented reasons tied to the injury, and the file is being kept open pending those records.

Entry 9: File status updated to pending medical review. No coverage issues identified at this time, and next step is to request the complete treatment records from counsel.
